---
title: "Agents"
---

Agents are custom **subagents** that Claude Code can delegate a task to via its
built-in `Agent` tool. Each `.claude/agents/<name>.md` file gives a subagent a
system prompt, a `description` (what Claude Code matches invocations against),
and a restricted `tools` list. Claude Code discovers agents in `.claude/agents/`
automatically — like skills, no separate registration step is needed once this
repo is bootstrapped.

## Why read-only fan-out workers

Several skills fan a task out across many independent targets — one competitor
community per research pass, one dependency pin per audit, one claim per
fact-check — and want each target checked in parallel without risking a stray
worker writing a file, filing an issue, or running a destructive command.
Every agent in this repo omits `Edit` and `Write` from its Claude Code
`tools` list.
Claude Code honors that allowlist (the `tools:` field, documented at
<https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents> and in this repo since
[ai-config#341](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/ai-config/pull/341);
still the mechanism Claude Code uses as of 2026-08-26).
Some other harnesses still grant Write schemas to the same persona
(Cursor Cloud Task, measured 2026-08-25 PDT on
[ai-config#2265](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/ai-config/pull/2265),
[ai-config#2266](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/ai-config/pull/2266), and
[ai-config#2272](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/ai-config/pull/2272)),
so the restriction is not a universal harness guarantee.
All but one of them also keep `Bash`, which *can* run write-capable shell
commands (`git push`, `rm`, a redirect); for those, staying read-only is
instruction-level discipline, not a harness guarantee (see the note below the
table). Each agent returns a report.
The calling session dispositions findings and applies fixes,
even when a harness still grants the worker Write schemas,
on the user's go-ahead.

`adversarial-reviewer` is the one that is not a fan-out worker but a **critic**
--- it reviews the calling session's own diff rather than investigating the
repo fresh.
The read-only constraint matters for the same reason and one more:
a reviewer that could edit would turn a finding into a silent fix, losing the
finding and its disposition together.

| [`dependency-auditor`](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/ai-config/blob/main/.claude/agents/dependency-auditor.md) | `Bash`, `Read`, `Grep`, `Glob`, `WebFetch` | [`check-dependency-updates`](skills/check-dependency-updates/SKILL.md) (`cdu`) | Surveys pinned GitHub Actions tags/SHAs, `renv.lock` versions, pre-commit revs, Quarto/tool versions in CI, and submodules for available upgrades, reads changelogs, and reports what each bump would buy |
| [`hallucination-detector`](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/ai-config/blob/main/.claude/agents/hallucination-detector.md) | `Bash`, `Read`, `Grep`, `Glob`, `WebFetch` | [`purge-hallucinations`](skills/purge-hallucinations/SKILL.md) (`ph`) | Verifies concrete, checkable references --- files, functions, action refs, URLs, citations, config keys --- against ground truth and sorts each into Resolves / Fabricated / Unverifiable |

| [`skill-usage-auditor`](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/ai-config/blob/main/.claude/agents/skill-usage-auditor.md) | `Bash`, `Read`, `Grep`, `Glob` | [`skill-audit`](skills/skill-audit/SKILL.md) | Enumerates skills, greps local session transcripts for their invocations, rolls alias counts into their canonical skill, and buckets every skill into actively-used / dormant / dead |

Every agent except `community-demand-scout` keeps `Bash` for read-only checks
(`grep`, `gh api`, `git submodule status`, `test -e`) --- avoiding a
write-capable shell command (`renv::update()` without `check = TRUE`,
`pre-commit autoupdate`) is instruction-level discipline for those.
Each such agent's file under `.claude/agents/` says so in as many words,
so the Bash discipline is instructed where it is relied on rather than
only asserted here.
The Claude Code versus other-harness split for `Edit`/`Write` is in
[Why read-only fan-out workers](#why-read-only-fan-out-workers) above.
`adversarial-reviewer` is the persona that currently carries the
Write-schema hedge.
The `.opencode/` mirrors are not all the same: opencode's own permission block
can deny `bash` outright, in which case that surface is
harness-enforced there.
A harness that still grants Write schemas is not bound by that block.
Which copy Cursor Cloud reads was not isolated
(measured 2026-08-25 PDT).

## How they're invoked

The calling skill fans work out to one of these agents through Claude Code's
`Agent` tool, passing a scope line — what to check, against what — rather than
letting the agent pick its own scope. To use one standalone rather than through
its usual skill, invoke the `Agent` tool with `subagent_type` set to the
agent's name and describe the single target to check.
